newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slashes loss thanks to technology shares.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slashes loss thanks to technology shares.

text.p: A powerhouse showing from some major over-the-counter high techs, including industry giant Intel Corp, helped Nasdaq slash its losses by Wednesday's close.

Nasdaq had joined in the overall rout in the stock market after bonds tumbled on comments by Goldman Sachs International Vice Chairman Robert Hormats, who said he thought the appetite could wane among Japanese institutions for U.S. Treasuries.

The Nasdaq Composite Index finished down 3.43 points unofficially, or 0.26 percent, at 1309.12 after having sunk as low as 1269.94. Losers led gainers by 2953 to 1421 on volume of about 642 million shares.
Intel led the charge higher, closing up 7-3/4 at 136-7/8. The company said its chipmaking factories are at full production, a sign that sales of the company's popular semiconductors are robust.
Merrill Lynch raised its 1997 Intel earnings per share forecast to $9.00 from $7.70.
Also higher was Cascade Communications Corp, which rose five to 66-7/8. Morgan Stanley raised its rating on the stock to strong buy from buy.
